title: The Blue Room in Los Angeles and his nephew's piano playing
summary: He owned the Blue Room at 99th and Central for three or four years in the war; his nephew Jerry Bryant played piano.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: So, I worked there for two...three weeks. Then I left outa Chicago, an' I came back to California. I brought my wife out here in California. So that was when I had the joint they called the Blue Room.
How long did you have that place?

Oh, three...four years. It was durin' a wartime an', uh, had a place down the street called Honey Murphy's. When you go out there at night, 'd be so many Yellow Cabs out there, you'd thought it was a depot or the airport.
What was going on at Honey Murphy's?

He had a show...a bar there. Had his show... had girls in the joint, an' all the sailors and soldiers used to come down in San Diego an' around would come up there and come to California to have a ball. So they come up there and they'd have a good time. 'Course an' in that same time, I lived at Ninety-Ninth and Central, upstairs over my joint.
Did you have entertainment in your joint?
Yeah, I had my nephew. My nephew, my sister's son, he played the piano for me. He lives in Canada now.
Jerry Bryant. He was born on an Easter mornin'. We call him Jerry Easter Bryant.
He got another...he got a brother called Merle Bryant. He was over here th'other day.
